topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: From tumor viruses to cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how investigations of cancer-causing viruses established that transformation can originate in altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether a gene or mutation produces transformed cellular behavior.

topics.label: Cancer-gene classification and mutation-specific effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects and why their actual behavior depends on the affected protein and the particular mutation.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish the major forms of genetic instability and explain how failures of DNA repair generate them.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how faulty genome copying or segregation generates instability that can promote tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing and order of mutation acquisition influence progression from normal colorectal tissue to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Inherited cancer predisposition and the changing role of BRCA2 deficiency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited defects accelerate tumor development, with BRCA2 restoration showing that an initiating defect need not remain necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture close and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading, and announcing the next lecture.
